assessments.reasoning: OpenVPN/openvpn publishes the captured COPYING at 9779cef26e296bb7c94e336c0a1ea1f4da3276d9 with the claim’s SHA-256. Bytes [497,1217) place the GPL version statement, named exception, grantor and operative conditions within the OpenVPN component notice.

The License Index SCOPE.md at cdff8aeed68bf1f9c62d8c86159c7dc08b2d75d7 includes historical editions. Its exception row, bytes [640,783), applies to the additional linking permission expressly granted in this component notice. A separate base-edition claim would require its own support.

challenge.method: Under pinned SCES-1.0 §§1, 3–4 and Protocol stage 7, I compared the grantor, linked components and operative terms under the OpenVPN and LZO headings, then checked the separate toolkit license for a possible publisher mix-up.
challenge.results: OpenVPN Technologies grants the OpenVPN–OpenSSL permission in the OpenVPN license section. Markus F.X.J. Oberhumer separately grants the OpenVPN project permission to link LZO with OpenSSL. The toolkit’s own OpenSSL and SSLeay terms appear later. These adjacent provisions have different grantors and subjects.

limitations: The grant covers OpenSSL and modified versions using the same license. It requires GPL compliance for the other code and gives modifiers a choice about extending the exception.

The GPL version 2 statement concerns the OpenVPN component. Other bundled material has separate notices. The review uses the supplied 2.3.18 commit and content pin. The COPYING text itself does not print the release number.
reasoning: The pinned OpenVPN COPYING names OpenVPN Technologies, Inc. as grantor under “Special exception for linking OpenVPN with OpenSSL.” It permits linking and distribution of linked combinations, meeting the Index additional-permission criterion. “Historical” describes the Index’s OpenVPN 2.3.18 reference and carries no finding that the grant has expired.
